components.name: The Gnomon
components.description: The mark: a sun, an upright and the shadow it casts on the threshold, beside the lowercase wordmark. Its colours come from --mark-*, which no accent sheet sets.
components.html: Umbral
components.css: .ds-brand { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; } .ds-mark { width: 28px; height: 28px; } .ds-mark-sun { fill: var(--mark-sun, #f5c26b); } .ds-mark-base { stroke: var(--mark-base, #3a3a52); } .ds-mark-shadow { fill: var(--mark-shadow, #a7a2b6); opacity: var(--mark-shadow-opacity, 0.5); } .ds-mark-upright { stroke: var(--mark-upright, #ece8df); } .ds-wordmark { font-family: var(--font-display, 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'Schibsted Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif); font-weight: 800; font-size: 24px; line-height: 32px; letter-spacing: -0.035em; text-transform: lowercase; color: var(--color-on-surface, #ece8df); }

narrative.overview:
Umbral means threshold; an umbra is the shadow a thing casts. The mark draws exactly that: a sun, an upright, and the shadow it casts on a threshold line. The identity providers are the light, Umbral stands in it, and every app receives the same shadow. The whole look follows from the mark: a field of ink (or, in the light theme, of warm paper), a single corona of gold for what matters, and nothing else that asks for attention.

The product is a tool the operator opens a few times a year and a page that other people pass through in seconds. Both want the same thing: quiet, exact surfaces where the one gold element is the one to act on. Density is moderate, line lengths are short, and everything that is not text is either a tonal step of the background or a one-pixel line. The light theme is not an inversion but the same scene by day: paper instead of ink, ink instead of bone, a darker gold that still reads as gold, and a primary button that becomes ink with gold text so the accent never has to carry dark type.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, used sparingly: gold for the primary action, links, focus and the current place, and for nothing decorative.
Two themes always, chosen by the system unless the person picks one; the first paint is already in the right theme.
Depth by tone and hairline, not by shadow.
Three faces with fixed jobs: a display face for headings and the wordmark, a text face for everything else, a mono face for anything a machine reads.
Pill buttons and softly rounded fields and cards; no sharp corners anywhere but the focus ring.
Everything self-hosted and legible with JavaScript off.

rules.name: The Fill Pair Rule
rules.body: The primary button uses primary-fill / on-primary-fill, not primary / on-primary. In the dark theme both pairs are gold on umber. In the light theme the fill pair is ink (#17151f) with gold text (#f5c26b) while links stay the darker gold (#8a5a00), so a gold fill never has to carry dark text at 4.5:1. An app's accent sheet overrides both pairs and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Red Fill Rule
rules.body: On any card, at most one button has the red danger fill, and it is the action that cannot be undone (Delete app, Delete connector). A destructive action that can be undone, such as removing a logo that can be uploaded again, is a ghost button in the error colour.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: Spec 007 FR-007: every text at 4.5:1 or better against what it sits on, every input border and focus indicator at 3:1 or better, in both themes. Where a palette value misses this for a border, the plan records a darker (light) or lighter (dark) value of the same hue for that use. An app's accent is checked against both themes and saved with a warning, never refused; its button text is black or white, whichever reads better, chosen by Umbral.

rules.name: The Mark Keeps Its Colours
rules.body: The Gnomon takes its colours from --mark-*, which no accent rule touches, so an app's colour never recolours Umbral's mark. The "Secured by Umbral" line cannot be hidden or recoloured.

rules.name: The Lowercase Wordmark Rule
rules.body: The wordmark reads umbral, in the display face at 800 with -0.035em tracking, lowercased by CSS so the text stays "Umbral" for titles and screen readers.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Anything a person will copy into a configuration file or compare character by character is set in the mono face.

rules.name: The Catalogue Rule
rules.body: Every word on a page comes from Views/Texts.fs. When a mockup and the catalogue disagree, the catalogue wins.

rules.name: The Flat Rest Rule
rules.body: No shadow on a surface at rest. A shadow, if one ever appears, answers a state: something lifted, dragged or floating.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line in outline-variant, often at 40% (border-outline-variant/40) for the rail's edge, the name bar and the footer. Thicker lines appear only as the 2px focus ring and the 2px crop box.

dos: Do take every colour, size and radius from the tokens (bg-primary, text-on-surface-variant, rounded-lg), so both themes and an app's accent sheet keep working.
Do write class names as literal strings in views; the Tailwind scanner reads Views/ and Handlers/ and cannot see a name built by interpolation.
Do regenerate umbral.css with src/Umbral/Assets/build-css.sh after touching a view, the tokens or umbral.input.css, and commit it; CI and the image build run --check and fail on a stale file.
Do check every new surface at 1280px and 360px in both themes, with the system theme and with a chosen one.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 and borders and focus at 3:1 in both themes, and measure from the tokens, not by eye.
Do make every control work with JavaScript off and every form carry the antiforgery token; a destructive form carries data-confirm.
Do put a new reusable look into .um-* in umbral.input.css and a helper in Components.fs, not into a one-off class string.
Do take wording from Views/Texts.fs and add new strings there.
donts: Don't use a second accent, a gradient, a glow or a coloured shadow. Gold is the only colour that is not a tone of the surface or a status.
Don't put a shadow on a surface at rest.
Don't give a card more than one red-filled button, or fill red for an action that can be undone.
Don't set a colour on the Gnomon, hide or move "Secured by Umbral", or let an app's accent reach anything but the primary pairs.
Don't load a font, script, stylesheet, image or icon from another host; the Content-Security-Policy refuses it and the product promises it.
Don't put style="" in markup; the policy allows inline style only when a script writes it.
Don't use the display face below headline large, or the mono face for prose.
Don't build a menu or a drawer for the rail; it wraps on narrow screens by design.
